title: Checkpoint: World 2
objectives: Apply everything learned in World 2 (symbols, linear flowcharts, reverse translation, mistakes, building flowcharts) together

hook.text: You have reached the end of World 2. Now it is time to test your flowchart reading and drawing skills with mixed questions.

concept.heading: Checkpoint
concept.body: This lesson does not teach a new topic; it reinforces what you have learned. The questions below test symbol recognition, reading flowcharts, building flowcharts, and common mistakes in a mix.

exercises.question: Build the flowchart for the algorithm "calculate double a number and print it".
What is the state of a flowchart if the "No" branch of a decision symbol is not connected to anything?
options: Invalid: the branch is left hanging

feedback.correct: Correct. An unconnected branch leaves the flow unclear.
feedback.incorrect: Every decision branch must lead somewhere, otherwise the flowchart is invalid.

exercises.question: Complete the sentence.
exercises.template: The IF command is shown in a flowchart with the ___ symbol.

exercises.question: At most how many arrows can leave a process symbol?

feedback.correct: Correct. A process symbol must have a single exit.
feedback.incorrect: A process symbol can have only one exit; more than one requires a decision symbol.

exercises.question: Put the pseudocode steps of the algorithm "calculate the cube of a number" in the correct order.
Which of these two commands can the parallelogram symbol in a flowchart stand for?

feedback.correct: Correct. The input/output symbol matches the READ or WRITE commands.
feedback.incorrect: The parallelogram symbol stands for one of the READ or WRITE commands.

summary: World 2 complete: flowchart symbols, linear flowcharts, reverse translation, common mistakes, building flowcharts.
These skills will be used from World 3 onward to read and draw flowcharts for decision structures.
You will see the topics you struggled with again in your review queue.
